disclaimer: Olympiad rules, dates and eligibility change. This page records what the official sources said on the check date. Confirm with the organiser before relying on a date or entry rule.
intro: Each subject has its own national route. The stages below are the usual progression; the official organiser controls registration, rounds and team selection. TEMS prepares students for the problem style at each stage but does not select national teams.

subjects.subject: Mathematics
subjects.tagline: BdMO → national round → IMO and APMO
subjects.summary: The Bangladesh Mathematical Olympiad is the main national route, with regional rounds feeding a national stage. The strongest students may be invited to selection camps for the IMO, and Bangladesh also competes in the Asia-Pacific Mathematics Olympiad.

stages.name: School & regional
stages.description: The BdMO season runs from December to February. School and regional rounds are the usual entry point; the official site publishes the current registration route for each class.

stages.name: National
stages.description: Regional winners and high scorers progress to the national round. The BdMO is open to students from Class I to Class XII, so the national stage spans primary through higher secondary.

stages.name: Selection
stages.description: National winners and awardees may be invited to training and selection camps for international teams. Selection is controlled by the organiser, not by any coaching academy.

stages.name: International
stages.description: Bangladesh sends a team to the International Mathematical Olympiad and competes in the Asia-Pacific Mathematics Olympiad. Both are proof-based competitions.

international.name: IMO
international.note: Six problems over two days. National teams are selected through each country’s official route.
international.eligibility: Under 20 and not enrolled in tertiary education.

international.name: APMO
international.note: Five problems in four hours. Bangladesh competes in the Asia-Pacific region.
international.eligibility: Students from participating Asia-Pacific countries and regions.

subjects.subject: Physics
subjects.tagline: BdPhO → national selection → IPhO and APhO
subjects.summary: The Bangladesh Physics Olympiad is the national route. It feeds selection for the International Physics Olympiad and the Asian Physics Olympiad. Both international competitions test theory and experimental work.

stages.name: School & regional
stages.description: BdPhO publishes its current registration and round structure each season. School and regional rounds are the usual first stage.

stages.name: National
stages.description: Successful students progress to the national BdPhO round, where problems require physical modelling rather than recall.

stages.name: Selection
stages.description: National performers may be invited to team selection and training. The BdPhO organiser controls the process.

stages.name: International
stages.description: Bangladesh sends a team to the International Physics Olympiad and competes in the Asian Physics Olympiad.

international.name: IPhO
international.note: A theoretical and an experimental paper. Each national team is limited to five students, with two leaders.
international.eligibility: Secondary school students selected by their national organisation.

international.name: APhO
international.note: A regional physics competition with up to eight contestants per participating country.
international.eligibility: Secondary school students from participating Asian countries.

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.summary: The Bangladesh Chemistry Olympiad is run through the Bangladesh Chemical Society. Strong national performers may be selected for the International Chemistry Olympiad, which combines theory with practical chemistry.

stages.name: School & regional
stages.description: The Bangladesh Chemical Society publishes the current BChO registration route and round structure. School and regional stages are the usual entry point.

stages.name: National
stages.description: The national BChO round tests inorganic, organic and physical chemistry beyond the school syllabus.

stages.name: Selection
stages.description: National awardees may be invited to selection and training for the international team. The chemical society controls selection.

stages.name: International
stages.description: Bangladesh participates in the International Chemistry Olympiad, which includes theoretical and practical examinations.

international.name: IChO
international.note: The official steering committee site lists the current host, programme and regulations.
international.eligibility: Secondary school students selected by their national organisation.

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.summary: The Bangladesh Biology Olympiad is the national route to the International Biology Olympiad. IBO preparation rewards careful data interpretation and structure–function reasoning as much as factual recall.

stages.name: School & regional
stages.description: BDBO publishes its registration and round structure each season. School and regional rounds are the usual first stage.

stages.name: National
stages.description: The national BDBO round tests cell biology, genetics, physiology, ecology and evolution beyond the textbook.

stages.name: Selection
stages.description: National awardees may be invited to selection and training. The BDBO organiser controls the process.

stages.name: International
stages.description: Bangladesh participates in the International Biology Olympiad, which combines theoretical and practical tasks.

international.name: IBO
international.note: The official site publishes regulations, hosts and results. The past-paper archive is password-protected for teachers.
international.eligibility: Secondary school students selected by their national organisation.

subjects.subject: Junior science
subjects.summary: Junior science has two international routes. The Bangladesh Junior Science Olympiad feeds a six-member IJSO team through registration, regional or online rounds, a national round and a national camp. IMSO is the younger international route for mathematics and science.

stages.name: Registration
stages.description: Students register through the Bangladesh Junior Science Olympiad. The official route begins with registration, followed by regional or online rounds.

stages.name: Regional or online
stages.description: The first competitive stage is a regional or online round, depending on the cycle. The BdJSO publishes the format.

stages.name: National & camp
stages.description: Successful students progress to the national round and then a national camp. The camp prepares the team for the international competition.

stages.name: International
stages.description: Bangladesh sends a six-member team to the International Junior Science Olympiad. The 2026 IJSO is in Bulgaria. IMSO is a separate international route for younger students.

international.name: IJSO
international.note: Integrated science: physics, chemistry and biology. Bangladesh’s route runs through BdJSO and a national camp.
international.eligibility: Under 16 on the competition’s cut-off date; confirm the current rule with the organiser.

international.name: IMSO
international.note: A mathematics and science competition for younger students, with national delegations.
international.eligibility: Under 13; confirm the current rule with the organiser.
